title: The Economy of the Flesh
english: The economy of the flesh: For I was led like a sheep to the slaughter and like a lamb before its shearer, silent. Since the devil was attacking me, wanting to snatch my flesh like a sheep, but knowing that the Divinity, as a shepherd, withdraws and flees, because of this I hide the Divinity like a shepherd, but I present my flesh like a sheep, so that, emboldened, he might approach, and having approached, might snatch, and having snatched my flesh like a sheep, he might be destroyed by the two-edged sword of the Spirit (Heb 4:12). Stop then, heretic, my cowardice and my ignorance which you are disparaging. For I act cowardly so that I may show the incomprehensible taking up of the flesh.

I say: My soul is troubled, so that you may learn that I have not taken up an insensate body, as the Apollinarian error wills. Do not then cast the sufferings of the flesh upon the impassible by word: for I am God and man, heretic. As God, he guarantees the wonders; as man, he witnesses the sufferings. Since therefore I am God and man, say, who is the one suffering? If God suffered, you have said the blasphemous thing; but if the flesh suffered, why do you attach the suffering to that [the Divinity] to which you do not attribute cowardice? For when another is suffering, another does not act cowardly, and a God being crucified is not disturbed.

And that the flesh suffered, while the Word remained impassible, is witnessed by Isaiah, who, having seen me drenched in spirit, asked: Why are your garments red? (Isa 1:18). Your garments, he says, are red, and not you. For the body indeed is stained, but the Word of the Divinity is not harmed. And also witness is Jacob the patriarch, saying concerning me: He washes his robe in wine and his garment in the blood of the grape (Gen 49:14). What robe? The body. With what blood? That which flowed from the side. But if not

title: The distinction between human fear and divine impotence
english: You cast my testimony aside, but I testify to myself. For my testimony is true, even if you do not wish it, which I used to say to the Jews: 'Why do you want to kill me, a man who has spoken the truth to you?' 'A man,' he said, 'heretic, not God.'

This man, Jesus, who was killed by the Jews, fears. And do not disturb the word with your ignorance. For this reason I fear, so that death might cling to me as a man, and be defeated as being from God. But even while fearing, I do not entirely decline the passion. For if I had declined, I would not have said: 'Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me' (Matt 26:39). For it is certain that nothing is impossible for the Father.

If indeed I asked that death be brought forward, but He did not bring it about, you raise two absurdities. For if, being unable, He did not bring it forward, or if, being stingy, He handed it over, you would find, heretic, that you are attributing cowardice to me and impotence to the Father. But while saying I am a coward, you ask forgiveness on account of the flesh, yet while rubbing against the Father's impotence, you err unpardonably, saying the power of God is weaker than death. Otherwise, you would make me appear stronger than the Father.

And I state the manner. For if I, while living in the flesh, raised Lazarus, the daughter of Jairus, the boy of the widow, but having died again in the flesh, I emptied the tombs of the five hundred dead, my Father, having experienced neither flesh nor death, would say of me, the one whom He loved as a child, as He himself says: 'This is my beloved Son' (Matt 3:17), [that] to come out of dangers He was not able—see what you suffer, heretic. Because you do not give equal judgment to what is equal to me, you provide more unwillingly, and whom you think is being dragged down by weakness, you make appear stronger than the Father; for I indeed and <not]

title: Victory over Hades
english: Having been called to rescue the souls held in Hades, I delivered them. For they say, 'Lord, you have brought my soul up from Hades,' yet having been called, he did not free my troubled soul from the attachments of evils.

But may it never be! For neither the father, being either ungenerous or powerless, failed to free me from the suffering, nor did I, while refusing the suffering, ask for the cup to pass. For if suffering is unheard of, I truly was cowardly; but if death is arbitrary, I thought it cowardly to free man by using sophistry against the devil. Therefore, the devil, not agreeing with this, dragged me as if to drown me, unaware that he also had those whom he would have cast down by me.

As soon as I rushed upon Hades, I plundered its tombs and stripped the sarcophagi. I stripped them not by open fighting, but by invisibly providing the resurrection. For I loosed no one and all fled, I spoke nothing and liberty was proclaimed, I called no one and all rushed together. For as soon as I arrived as a king, the tyrant was despised, I shone as light and the darkness was dissolved.

For it was to see every prisoner seeing liberty, and every captive dancing the resurrection; thus, as those dead were marvelling at me in the victory, while casting down death in its defeat, saying: 'Where, O Death, is your sting? Where, O Hades, is your victory?' And these things are so. Let us send up glory for the things said to Christ, the King of all, for to him belong glory, honor, and worship, with the unblemished Father and the all-holy Spirit, unto the ages of ages. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
